Subject: RFP Appendix C: Commercial clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking Appendix C — a couple of clarifications from procurement before we proceed to legal:

1) Commit mechanics: the RFP asks for token-based commit tiers and a true-up cadence. Can you confirm whether unused committed tokens convert to account credits, rollover, or expire? If credits, what percentage of unused value is applied?

2) Overage pricing: do you support stepped overage discounts (e.g., lower per-token price after 100% of commit is consumed)? Any difference between standard hosted and Dedicated pools?

3) Proration & upgrades: how do upgrades mid-term get pro-rated? Downgrades?

4) Multi-year pricing: are there stretch discounts for 2-3 year commits, and do you offer price caps?

I'm attaching Appendix_C for reference. We're hoping to finalize commercial terms next week.

Attachments: Quantum_RFP_Appendix_C_Commercial.pdf

Samira —

Appreciate the clear questions. High-level response and attached pricing matrix; I'm happy to walk through numbers live. Key points: 

- Commit tiers: we propose three committed tiers (Silver/Gold/Platinum) with associated monthly token commitments. Commitments are per-quarter billing windows for predictability; you can annualize for a single invoice.

- Unused commit handling: unused committed tokens convert to account credits at 70% of their face value and apply to the next billing quarter automatically. Credits expire after 12 months unless covered by a multi-year agreement (see discounts).

- Overage structure: overage price is defined per-token and steps down at pre-agreed thresholds. Example: if you exceed commit by up to 25% the overage rate is +30% of base commit price; beyond 25% triggers the next step (lower per-token cost). Dedicated pools (Reserved/Dedicated) get a lower baseline overage rate and larger step-down bands because of capacity reservation.

- Proration and mid-term changes: upgrades are pro-rated immediately; downgrades are allowed only at quarter boundaries with 30 days' notice unless you elect an immediate downgrade at a cap fee.

- Multi-year: year-over-year discounts available (10% off list for year 2, 15% for year 3) subject to minimum annual commitment. Price caps can be negotiated for 24–36 month terms.

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_v3.xlsx (pricing matrix + worked examples).

Next step: if this aligns, we'll produce a commercial SOW and a DocuSign envelope for a 12/24/36-month commit option set.

Regards,

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: commit tiering and volume crediting framework (QINS-2026-78)

Samira / Procurement —

Thanks for the questions. Below is the formalized commercial position we propose for QINS-2026-78; I've included numerical examples to illustrate behavior in spike and downgrades. If you confirm, we'll convert this into a commercial SOW and send a DocuSign package (link below) for the indicated term options.

Commercial summary (key bullets):
- Commit tiers (monthly equivalent, invoiced quarterly):
  • Silver: 10M tokens/month (120M annual) — list base price $0.0009/ token on commit
  • Gold: 50M tokens/month (600M annual) — list base price $0.00065/ token on commit
  • Platinum: 200M tokens/month (2.4B annual) — list base price $0.00045/ token on commit

- Overage pricing (hosted):
  • 0–25% over commit: overage = base_commit_price * 1.30
  • 25–100% over commit: overage = base_commit_price * 1.10 (step-down after first band)
  • >100% over commit: negotiate enterprise add-on or auto-scale to Dedicated pricing

- Dedicated pools: baseline per-token is 15–25% lower (depending on reserved capacity) and step-down thresholds widen (first band to 50%). Exact figures in the attached Commitment_Tiers_Schedule.pdf.

- Unused commit credits: unused committed tokens are converted to account credits at 70% of committed token value for single-year agreements. For 2-year agreements we return 80%; for 3-year agreements 85%. Credits are applied automatically to the next billing quarter and expire after 12 months if not consumed.

- Proration rules:
  • Upgrades: immediate pro-rata credit applied to the effective date (you pay the delta for remainder of the quarter).
  • Downgrades: allowed only at quarter boundary with 30-day notice; immediate downgrade permitted with one-time fee equal to 10% of remaining quarter commit value.

- Multi-year discounts & price caps:
  • 2-year: additional 10% off list (applies to base_commit_price)
  • 3-year: additional 15% off list
  • Price caps: maximum 5% year-over-year CPI-based increases or the negotiated cap in the SOW (whichever lower).

- Early termination: buyout equals remaining committed value minus a 20% mitigation credit (i.e., customer pays 80% of remaining committed spend), capped at the committed remaining annual value. Assignment allowed with Redwood consent; consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

Worked example (spike month):
- Customer on Gold commit (50M/mo) at $0.00065/token. Quarterly invoice covers 150M tokens commit ($97,500).
- Month 2 spike to 120M tokens (70M over monthly commit). Overage calculation (first 25% band = up to 12.5M over the monthly commit):
  • First band (12.5M tokens) billed at 1.30 * $0.00065 = $0.000845/token => $10,562.50
  • Remaining overage (57.5M - 12.5M = 45M) billed at 1.10 * $0.00065 = $0.000715/token => $32,175.00
  • Total overage month = $42,737.50.
  • Unused credits from prior quarter (if any) are applied after overage is calculated; credit value = 70% * unused_token_value.

Example (unused credits):
- If prior quarter had 30M unused tokens at commit price $0.00065 => face value $19,500; credit applied = 70% * $19,500 = $13,650 applied to next invoice.

Operational notes:
- Private deployment SSO + KMS requirements add a fixed $Xk/mo platform security surcharge; Dedicated reserved capacity pricing to be modeled separately per capacity size.

Next steps: please confirm which term set you'd like (12/24/36) and whether you want Dedicated reserved capacity pricing modeled against your traffic profile. I'll have Legal prep a SOW and send the DocuSign envelope for signature.
